grants.Program Focus:
OPENING SUMMARY — WEEK OF SEPTEMBER 28 – OCTOBER 2, 2026

Small Business / Transportation Technical Assistance:

USDOT OSDBU Small Business Transportation Technical Assistance Center, Region 1 (OST/OSDBU-2027-SBTTAC-Region 1-FY2027-1) — one cooperative agreement of $377,016 to run the 11-state Northeast/Mid-Atlantic center (formerly SBTRC). 501(c)(3)/(c)(6) organizations with a Region 1 office only; 15% match, at least half in cash.

Due October 31, 2026 (a Saturday).

Transportation Planning:

FHWA Prioritization Process Pilot Program (FHWA-PPPP-26-001) — up to $26,000,000, max $2,000,000 per grant, federal share up to 100%. States and MPOs serving urbanized areas over 200,000 only. Due October 30, 2026.

Highway Safety / Wildlife Connectivity:

FHWA Wildlife Crossings Pilot Program FY 2026 (FHWA-WCPP-26-002) — approximately $80,000,000, no minimum or maximum award; 20% non-federal match; at least 60% to rural areas; construction projects may be prioritized. Public agencies, MPOs, Tribes, and FLMAs only. Due November 16, 2026.

Dairy / Agriculture:

USDA AMS Dairy Business Innovation Initiatives FY 2026 (USDA-AMS-TM-DBI-G-26-0011) — $12,650,000 across four awards of $2.3M–$3.45M. Applicant pool is closed to the four existing DBI initiatives; client access is through their subawards, with AMS steering this round toward equipment and infrastructure. Due December 1, 2026.

Agriculture / SBIR-STTR Phase II:

USDA NIFA SBIR/STTR Phase II (USDA-NIFA-SBIR-012221) — $24,750,000 this round ($19.5M SBIR, $5.25M STTR), up to $650,000 per award with TABA. Prior Phase I recipients only; one Phase II award per firm. Due November 17, 2026; a second round is set for September 21, 2027.

Rural Water / Solid Waste Technical Assistance:

USDA RUS Technical Assistance and Training FY 2027 (TAT-FY27) — approximately $35,000,000, no award cap. Private nonprofits only. Due December 31, 2026.

USDA RUS Solid Waste Management FY 2027 (SWMFY27) — approximately $4,000,000, up to $1,000,000 per award. Nonprofits, public bodies, Tribes, and academic institutions. Due December 31, 2026.

Basic Research / DOE Office of Science:

DOE Office of Science FY 2027 Open Call (DE-FOA-0003665) — approximately $400,000,000, $5,000–$10,000,000 per the listing, rolling through September 30, 2027. Open to all applicant types except DOE labs as leads; for-profits must show the work is fundamental research, not commercial. Topic-specific pre-application and target dates begin November 22, 2026.

Earth Science / Geohazards Research:

NASA ROSES-2025 A.18 Geosphere (NNH25ZDA001N-GEO) — new Earth Science element covering geohazard forecasting, resource extraction and surface deformation, critical mineral deposits, and core-to-surface energy flow. Funding level not posted on Grants.gov; no cost share. Mandatory Notice of Intent by November 16, 2026; no NOI, no review.

Proposals due January 15, 2027.

Community Development / Technical Assistance (Forecast):

HUD Distressed Cities Technical Assistance FY 2026–2027 (PDR-2700-DC-0054) — forecast of $5,000,000 across about six cooperative agreements of $400,000–$3,000,000 to deliver TA to local governments serving communities of 50,000 or fewer. Nonprofits, for-profits, and private universities only; no public entities.

Estimated due March 11, 2027; NOFO expected about January 11, 2027.

California State Opportunities:

CTC 2026 Local Partnership Competitive Program — $151,298,000 in SB 1 funds for jurisdictions with voter-approved or imposed transportation taxes or fees. 1:1 match required. Due November 18, 2026.

CTC 2026 Solutions for Congested Corridors Program — $500,000,000 for multimodal corridor projects nominated by RTPAs, county transportation commissions, and Caltrans. Projects must be in an adopted RTP and a comprehensive corridor plan. Due November 19, 2026.

CTC 2026 Trade Corridor Enhancement Program — $1,287,958,000 in state and federal funds for freight corridor improvements. Public entities including port authorities; 30% match. Due November 20, 2026.

Cal OES FY 2025 Next Generation Warning System for Early Earthquake Warning — $1.5M in total funding; up to $750,000 per award, one or two awards, federal funds paid on reimbursement. Streaming companies and their affiliates only. Due November 25, 2026.

Policy & Compliance Updates:

DOL ETA UIPL 15-26 — FY 2027 UI State Administration base planning targets, $2,632,033,000 across 53 jurisdictions. Formula funds to state workforce agencies; informational for clients.

EPA General Terms and Conditions effective October 1, 2026 — apply to new EPA awards and to existing awards when EPA next adds funds. Relevant to DERA National applicants from last week's digest.

EPA RAIN-2027-G01 — bars EPA funds, including cost share, from buying or operating FASC-prohibited drones, retroactive to December 22, 2025 and covering drones already in use on active awards.

National Academies Evaluation of ARPA-E's Mission and Goals — final report recommends reliable ARPA-E funding and tripling SCALEUP to $120M per year.

Watch List / Upcoming:

DOE SC open call — ASCR Analog Computing panel pre-applications due November 22, 2026; most BES white papers and pre-applications targeted for November 30, 2026; Electron and Scanning Probe Microscopies applications targeted for December 1, 2026.

SBTTAC — the NOFO puts total funding at $2.3M across six regions; watch for the other regional listings. The NOFO is internally inconsistent on the in-kind match cap (50% vs. 10%); confirm with SBTTAC@dot.gov before building a budget.

CTC SB 1 programs — three back-to-back deadlines November 18–20; awards expected June 2027. Pull the adopted 2026 guidelines from catc.ca.gov before scoping.

EPA drones — clients with active EPA awards that use drones should run and document the Consolidated Screening List check now.

RUS TAT and SWM — the NOFOs anticipate about 22 TAT and 15 SWM awards, while both listings show 40. Neither requires match, but 25% or more in non-federal resources is worth 15 points. Proposals must key each section to the NOFO criteria numbers.

NIFA SBIR/STTR Phase II — Phase I awardees not ready for November 17 can target the September 21, 2027 round (tentative).

grants.Description: U.S. Department of Transportation, OSDBU — FY 2027 Small Business Transportation Technical Assistance Center (SBTTAC), Region 1
grants.Opportunity #: OST/OSDBU-2027-SBTTAC-Region 1-FY2027-1 (Grants.gov FON OST-OSDBU-2027-SBTTAC-REGION1-FY2027-1); Assistance Listing 20.910 (Assistance to Small and Disadvantaged Businesses). Grants.gov opportunity 363996.
grants.Agency / Funder: U.S. Department of Transportation — Office of the Secretary, Office of Small and Disadvantaged Business Utilization (OSDBU). Program Manager Lynn Bailey, lynn.bailey@dot.gov; general inquiries to SBTTAC@dot.gov.
grants.Total Funding: $377,016 for Region 1, one of six regions sharing $2.3 million. One award.
grants.Award Range: $377,016 (single award). Ten-month base year with two option years, contingent on performance and funds.
grants.Eligible Applicants:
Established nonprofits, community-based organizations, transportation-related trade associations, chambers of commerce, colleges and universities, community colleges, and faith-based institutions; HBCUs are encouraged. Must be a 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(6), have an office physically located in a Region 1 state, and have at least one year of documented technical-assistance experience with small businesses in the region.

Region 1 covers Connecticut, Delaware, Maine, Maryland, Massachusetts, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, and Vermont. Staff must include a senior subject-matter expert with at least five years of transportation-contracting experience.

The Grants.gov listing also shows state governments as eligible; the NOFO does not. Treat the NOFO as controlling.
grants.Deadline:
October 31, 2026, 11:59 p.m. ET via Grants.gov. The deadline falls on a Saturday; plan to submit by Thursday, October 29.

A recorded NOFO information session (August 3, 2026) is linked from the listing.
grants.Program Focus:
Operating the regional technical-assistance hub that prepares small businesses to compete for federal, state, local, and private transportation contracts. Base-year KPIs are fixed:

• 67 capital-infusion transactions (loans, lines of credit, bonding, working capital);

• 1,665 hours of one-on-one counseling;

• 8 trainings, at least three in person and no more than one in the host state.

Review runs in three phases: merit review (Approach 25, Stakeholder Network 25, Organizational Capability 20, Cost 20, Risk/Compliance 10), a 60-minute presentation to OSDBU for Highly Recommended applicants, and Senior Review Team assessment. Applications are capped at 35 pages and must include a 2–3 page NSM-22 cybersecurity and physical-security risk plan.

This is the inaugural year under the SBTTAC name, so there is no prior-award history to model.
grants.Funding Instrument: Cooperative agreement; reimbursement only through DOT's Delphi eInvoicing system. No advances.
grants.Cost Share / Match:
Yes — 15% of the federal award in the base year, rising to 20% and 25% in the option years. At least half of the match must be cash.

The NOFO says up to 50% may be in-kind; the attached terms and conditions say no more than 10% may be in-kind. Confirm which governs before committing a match structure.
grants.Primary Sector: Small Business Technical Assistance; Transportation Contracting; Bonding and Capital Access; Procurement Readiness
grants.Link to NOFO: SBTTAC Region 1 on Simpler.Grants.gov; Region 1 FY2027 NOFO (PDF); Grants.gov listing

grants.Description: Federal Highway Administration — Prioritization Process Pilot Program (PPPP) Competitive Grant Program
grants.Opportunity #: FHWA-PPPP-26-001; Assistance Listing 20.262 (Prioritization Process Pilot Program). Grants.gov opportunity 364011.
grants.Agency / Funder: U.S. Department of Transportation — Federal Highway Administration. Listing contact is the Grants.gov Contact Center (1-800-518-4726, support@grants.gov); program contacts are in the NOFO.
grants.Total Funding: Up to $26,000,000, combining FY 2025 and FY 2026 funds with remaining FY 2024 funds. The listing's 100 expected awards is a placeholder; at the cap, the pool funds at least 13 awards.
grants.Award Range: Up to $2,000,000 per grant, the statutory maximum under IIJA § 11204(c)(3). No meaningful minimum.
grants.Eligible Applicants: States and metropolitan planning organizations serving a census-designated urbanized area with population over 200,000. No local governments, Tribes, or private entities as applicants.
grants.Deadline: October 30, 2026, 11:59 p.m. ET. FHWA anticipates announcing selections in March 2027.
grants.Program Focus:
IIJA pilot funding for States and large MPOs to develop and implement publicly accessible, data-driven processes for scoring and prioritizing projects in long-range transportation plans and transportation improvement programs.

A short-turnaround planning grant with no match is a good fit for MPO and State DOT clients that already have a prioritization framework in draft. FHWA posted an application template with the listing; start from it.
grants.Primary Sector: Transportation Planning; Project Prioritization; MPOs and State DOTs; IIJA

grants.Description: Federal Highway Administration — Fiscal Year 2026 Wildlife Crossings Pilot Program (WCPP)
grants.Opportunity #: FHWA-WCPP-26-002; Assistance Listing 20.290 (Wildlife Crossings Pilot Program). Grants.gov opportunity 364009.
grants.Agency / Funder: U.S. Department of Transportation — Federal Highway Administration. Listing contact is the Grants.gov Contact Center; program contacts are in the NOFO.
grants.Total Funding: Approximately $80,000,000 in FY 2026 funds, plus any remaining prior-year funds DOT elects to award. The listing shows 8 expected awards.
grants.Eligible Applicants: State DOTs; MPOs; units of local government; regional transportation authorities; special purpose districts or public authorities with a transportation function; Indian Tribes; Federal Land Management Agencies; or a group of any of these.
grants.Program Focus:
Projects that reduce wildlife-vehicle collisions and, in doing so, improve habitat connectivity for terrestrial and aquatic species. Both construction and non-construction projects are eligible, but DOT may prioritize construction.

By statute (23 U.S.C. 171(g)), at least 60% of each year's funds go to rural areas. The strongest candidates are rural crossing projects with collision data and design work already underway.
grants.Cost Share / Match: 20% non-federal share unless an exception applies; applicants without it are ineligible. FLMAs and Tribes may use other federal funds for their match, such as funds allowable under 23 U.S.C. 120(k).
grants.Primary Sector: Highway Safety; Wildlife-Vehicle Collision Reduction; Habitat Connectivity; Rural Transportation; Tribal Transportation
grants.Link to NOFO: WCPP on Simpler.Grants.gov; Final WCPP NOFO (PDF); Application template (DOCX); GrantSolutions announcement

grants.Description: USDA Agricultural Marketing Service — Dairy Business Innovation Initiatives Program (DBI), Fiscal Year 2026
grants.Opportunity #: USDA-AMS-TM-DBI-G-26-0011; Assistance Listing 10.176 (Dairy Business Innovation Initiatives). Grants.gov opportunity 364006.
grants.Agency / Funder: U.S. Department of Agriculture — Agricultural Marketing Service. Program questions to IPPGrants@usda.gov.
grants.Total Funding: Approximately $12,650,000, across four awards. For comparison, AMS awarded $11,040,000 to the same four initiatives in FY 2025.
grants.Eligible Applicants:
Closed list — only the four existing DBI initiatives may apply: the California State University Fresno Foundation, the University of Tennessee, the Vermont Agency of Agriculture, Food and Markets, and the University of Wisconsin.

Dairy farmers, processors, and other businesses participate as subaward recipients of these initiatives, not as direct applicants. For California clients, the route is the CSU Fresno Foundation initiative.
grants.Deadline: December 1, 2026, 11:59 p.m. ET (initiatives only). Subaward solicitations from each initiative will follow on their own schedules.
grants.Program Focus:
Diversifying dairy product markets and developing higher-value uses; business development that diversifies farmer income through processing and marketing innovation; and encouraging use of regional milk production.

AMS is strongly encouraging the initiatives to prioritize subawards for equipment and infrastructure in this round. Dairy processor clients with shovel-ready equipment or facility projects should get in front of the CSU Fresno initiative now and track its next subaward call.
grants.Cost Share / Match: The listing shows cost sharing as required. Confirm the requirement, and how it flows to subawardees, in the NOFO and the updated DBI Specific Terms and Conditions.
grants.Primary Sector: Dairy Processing; Value-Added Agriculture; Agricultural Equipment and Infrastructure; Regional Food Systems
grants.Link to NOFO: DBI on Simpler.Grants.gov; FY2026 DBI NOFO (PDF); DBI Specific Terms and Conditions (PDF); AMS DBI program page

grants.Description: USDA National Institute of Food and Agriculture — Small Business Innovation Research and Small Business Technology Transfer Programs Phase II (FY 2026 and FY 2027)
grants.Opportunity #: USDA-NIFA-SBIR-012221; Assistance Listing 10.212 (Small Business Innovation Research / Small Business Technology Transfer). Grants.gov opportunity 364020.
grants.Agency / Funder: U.S. Department of Agriculture — National Institute of Food and Agriculture (NIFA). Application questions to grantapplicationquestions@usda.gov; foreign-affiliation disclosure questions to sm.ddsbir@usda.gov.
grants.Total Funding:
$24,750,000 for the FY 2026 round: approximately $19,500,000 SBIR and $5,250,000 STTR. The same amounts are anticipated for the FY 2027 round, subject to appropriations.

The listing shows 50 expected awards; the NOFO's topic tables add up to 28 SBIR and 10 STTR awards per round.
grants.Award Range: Up to $600,000 without Technical and Business Assistance (TABA); $650,000 maximum with up to $50,000 of TABA. Projects normally run 24 months, up to 36 with justification. A fee of up to 7% is allowed within the ceiling. Budgets over the ceiling are returned without review.
grants.Eligible Applicants:
Prior SBIR/STTR Phase I recipients only, including novated or successor-in-interest recipients. Phase II continues the funded Phase I work, so confirm with NIFA before positioning a Phase I award from another agency.

Must be a for-profit small business concern with no more than 500 employees including affiliates, more than 50% owned and controlled by U.S. citizens or permanent residents (or qualifying small businesses, Alaska Native Corporations, Native Hawaiian Organizations, or Tribes). USDA does not accept majority-VC-owned firms. An SBA company registry SBC Control Number is required.

One Phase II application per Phase I award, at most two distinct applications per firm, and only one Phase II award per firm.
grants.Deadline:
FY 2026 round: November 17, 2026, 5:00 p.m. ET via Grants.gov (a Tuesday).

FY 2027 round: September 21, 2027 (tentative). Review takes about six months; the FY 2026 round's planned period of performance is March 15, 2027 through March 14, 2029. NIFA withholds Phase II funds until the preceding Phase I is complete.
grants.Program Focus:
Continuing Phase I research toward commercialization. Ten topic areas:

• 8.1 Forests and Related Resources; 8.2 Plant Production and Protection–Biology; 8.3 Animal Production and Protection;

• 8.4 Management of Natural Resources; 8.5 Food Science and Nutrition; 8.6 Rural and Community Development;

• 8.7 Aquaculture; 8.8 Biofuels and Biobased Products; 8.12 Small and Mid-Size Farms; 8.13 Plant Production and Protection–Engineering.

Cross-cutting priorities are agricultural-related manufacturing technology and biofuels and rural energy, including hydrogen and other fuel gases from agricultural waste. Topic 8.6 need not be agriculture-centered if the benefit is to rural Americans.

Scoring: Phase I results and feasibility 20, Phase II technical approach 20, commercial potential 20, importance 10, team 10, budget 10, non-duplication 10. A CRADA with a federal lab or a Phase III follow-on funding commitment breaks ties. Limits are a 20-page narrative, a 10-page commercialization plan, and a 250-word summary. Every applicant must file the foreign-affiliation disclosure form, even with nothing to disclose.
grants.Cost Share / Match:
None. Cost share is encouraged but not scored.

STTR requires a single partnering research institution to perform at least 30% of the work, with a formal IP allocation agreement.
grants.Primary Sector: Agricultural Technology; Food Science and Nutrition; Forestry and Natural Resources; Biofuels and Biobased Products; Small Business R&D
grants.Link to NOFO: SBIR/STTR Phase II on Simpler.Grants.gov; FY2026 Phase II NOFO (PDF); NIFA program page; Grants.gov listing

category: Rural Water, Wastewater, and Solid Waste

grants.Description: USDA Rural Utilities Service — Rural Water and Wastewater Technical Assistance and Training (TAT) Grants Program, Fiscal Year 2027
grants.Opportunity #: SWMFY27; Assistance Listing 10.762 (Solid Waste Management Grants). Grants.gov opportunity 364018.
grants.Agency / Funder: U.S. Department of Agriculture — Rural Development, Rural Utilities Service (RUS), Water and Environmental Programs. Contact Sandra Alarcón, Water-RD@usda.gov.
grants.Total Funding: Approximately $4,000,000, based on FY 2026 levels and dependent on FY 2027 appropriations. The NOFO anticipates about 15 awards.
grants.Award Range: No minimum. No award may exceed 25% of available funds, which is $1,000,000 at the anticipated level and matches the listing's maximum.
grants.Eligible Applicants:
Private nonprofits with IRS tax-exempt status, public bodies, federally acknowledged or state-recognized Tribes, and academic institutions. Private businesses, federal agencies, and individuals are ineligible. This is a broader pool than TAT.

Applicants must show a track record and actual capacity to deliver regional technical assistance. No more than 49% of the grant may go to a nonaffiliated contractor, and a proposal using less than 50% grantee or affiliated staff is ineligible.
grants.Deadline: December 31, 2026, 11:59 p.m. ET via Grants.gov (a Thursday). The window opened October 1. Awards are anticipated September 1, 2027 for a performance period of October 1, 2027 through September 30, 2028.
grants.Program Focus:
Technical assistance and training to reduce or eliminate pollution of water resources from rural solid waste sites:

• reducing the waste stream through reduction, recycling, and reuse;

• training operators of active landfills;

• closure, future land-use, safety, and maintenance planning for landfills that are closed or closing;

• evaluating landfill conditions for threats to water resources.

Proposals must show how the work supports site financial and operational sustainability (including capital financing applications), addresses emerging contaminants such as PFAS, or promotes household hazardous waste collection (electronics, pharmaceuticals). Funds cannot pay for construction or operation of facilities, real estate, or vehicles.

Scoring mirrors TAT: small, low-income target areas, 12-month projects, hands-on assistance, and up to 15 Administrator points through a separate "Administrator Points" section. Same 20-page proposal and 50-page package limits.
grants.Cost Share / Match: None required, but non-federal resources of 25% or more earn 15 points; 10–24.99% earns 10 and 1–9.99% earns 5.
grants.Primary Sector: Solid Waste and Recycling; Landfill Management and Closure; PFAS; Household Hazardous Waste; Rural Technical Assistance
grants.Link to NOFO: SWM on Simpler.Grants.gov; FY27 SWM NOFO (PDF); FY27 SWM Application Guide (PDF); RD program page; Grants.gov listing

grants.Description: U.S. Department of Energy, Office of Science — FY 2027 Continuation of Solicitation for the Office of Science Financial Assistance Program
grants.Opportunity #: DE-FOA-0003665; Assistance Listing 81.049 (Office of Science Financial Assistance Program). Grants.gov opportunity 363993.
grants.Agency / Funder: U.S. Department of Energy — Office of Science (SC). Administrative questions (budgets, eligibility) to sc.opencall@doe.gov; technical questions to the subprogram contacts named in the NOFO.
grants.Total Funding: Approximately $400,000,000 in current and future fiscal year funds, subject to appropriations. No stated number of awards.
grants.Award Range: $5,000 to $10,000,000 per the listing. Project periods run six months to five years, most commonly three. Several topic panels cap requests at $500,000 per year for three years and expect at most two awards.
grants.Eligible Applicants:
All applicant types, except 501(c)(4) organizations that have lobbied since 1995. DOE/NNSA National Laboratories cannot lead but may be subrecipients; non-DOE FFRDCs and other federal agencies may apply. Entities of Concern are barred.

For-profit applicants must attach a statement (200 words max) explaining how the work advances fundamental scientific understanding. Applications tied to current commercial activity or customer needs may be declined without review.
grants.Deadline:
Rolling through September 30, 2027, 11:59 p.m. ET, or until superseded. Topic-specific dates matter for FY 2027 consideration, for example:

• ASCR Analog Computing panel — pre-application November 22, 2026; application January 24, 2027.

• Most BES subprograms — white papers or pre-applications by November 30, 2026; applications by February 1, 2027.

• BES Electron and Scanning Probe Microscopies — applications by December 1, 2026.

Applications after a target date may roll to a later funding cycle.
grants.Program Focus:
SC's annual open call across six programs: Advanced Scientific Computing Research, Basic Energy Sciences, Biological and Environmental Research, Fusion Energy Sciences, High Energy and Nuclear Physics, and Isotope R&D and Production. Any research within SC's authorized mission may be proposed.

The NOFO lists dozens of subprograms with stated priorities and exclusions, including AI for science, quantum information science, critical-materials alternatives, fusion materials, and robotics and lab automation. Early contact with the subprogram manager is strongly encouraged and, for some panels, effectively required.

Best fit is university and nonprofit research clients. For company clients, only basic research framed around a "why" question will be competitive.
grants.Funding Instrument: Grants, cooperative agreements, interagency agreements, or Other Transaction Authority awards (including Technology Investment Agreements).
grants.Cost Share / Match: None for grants and cooperative agreements under 2 CFR 200 or 910 (basic research exclusion). OTA awards carry a 50% cost-share expectation to the maximum extent practicable.
grants.Primary Sector: Basic Energy Research; Scientific Computing and AI; Quantum Information Science; Fusion; Materials and Chemistry; Isotopes
grants.Link to NOFO: DE-FOA-0003665 on Simpler.Grants.gov; NOFO Part 1 (PDF); NOFO Part 2 (PDF); Office of Science

grants.Description: NASA Science Mission Directorate — ROSES-2025 Program Element A.18 Geosphere
grants.Opportunity #: NNH25ZDA001N-GEO (ROSES-2025 Amendment 77); Assistance Listing 43.001 (Science). Grants.gov opportunity 364021.
grants.Agency / Funder: National Aeronautics and Space Administration, Science Mission Directorate, Earth Science Division (NASA Headquarters). Program contact Thorsten Markus, thorsten.markus@nasa.gov, 202-358-3860. General ROSES questions to sara@nasa.gov.
grants.Eligible Applicants:
Proposers must be affiliated with an institution registered in NSPIRES. ROSES is generally open to all organization types, for-profit and nonprofit, though NASA generally funds only U.S. institutions; non-U.S. organizations participate on a no-exchange-of-funds basis.

Under the ROSES-25 Earth Science (Appendix A) restriction, federal agencies other than NASA and FFRDCs other than JPL do not receive funding.
grants.Deadline:
Mandatory Notice of Intent due November 16, 2026 via NSPIRES. Proposals due January 15, 2027. Any proposal without an on-time NOI will be returned without review.

Submission defaults to NSPIRES; Grants.gov submission is available only if requested at least 30 days before the due date.
grants.Program Focus:
New Earth Science element. Geosphere is one of the research "spheres" that replaced the Earth Science Division's prior focus areas. Proposals address one or more of four sub-elements:

• Geohazard forecasting and impact: volcanic deformation, pre-seismic monitoring and modeling, and hazard cascades (for example, earthquakes triggering tsunamis or landslides). Work on infrastructure or population impacts should tie to Earth Science to Action objectives.

• Resource extraction and deformation: process links between natural and human extraction from subsurface reservoirs and surface deformation.

• Critical mineral deposits and crustal processes: analysis or modeling of economically relevant deposits, referenced to the Final 2025 List of Critical Minerals; airborne and orbital assets may be used.

• Energy flow from core to surface: observations or models of deep-earth energy flow, with links to volcanic plume structure and geochemical tracers encouraged.

Client fit is as a partner or co-investigator with a research institution, particularly for geothermal, subsurface-resource, critical-mineral, and California seismic-hazard work.
grants.Primary Sector: Earth Science Research; Geohazards (Earthquakes, Volcanoes, Landslides, Tsunamis); Critical Minerals; Subsurface Resources
grants.Link to NOFO: A.18 Geosphere on Simpler.Grants.gov; NASA Amendment 77 announcement; NSPIRES program element; Grants.gov listing

grants.Description: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development — Distressed Cities Technical Assistance (DCTA) Program for Fiscal Years 2026 and 2027 (Forecast)
grants.Opportunity #: PDR-2700-DC-0054 (forecast); Assistance Listing 14.259 (Community Compass Technical Assistance and Capacity Building). Grants.gov opportunity 364022.
grants.Agency / Funder: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development. All communication goes to distressedcities@hud.gov.
grants.Award Range: $400,000–$3,000,000. The $3M ceiling against a $5M total suggests one large award alongside several small ones; confirm when the NOFO posts.
grants.Eligible Applicants:
Small businesses and other for-profit organizations; nonprofits with or without 501(c)(3) status; and private institutions of higher education. State and local governments, Tribes, and public universities are not listed. Individuals, foreign entities, and sole proprietorships are ineligible.

Awardees deliver TA to Units of General Local Government (UGLGs) serving communities of 50,000 or fewer people facing economic hardship; those governments are beneficiaries, not applicants.
grants.Deadline: Forecast only. Estimated NOFO posting January 11, 2027; estimated application due date March 11, 2027; estimated award April 30, 2027; estimated project start May 28, 2027.
grants.Program Focus:
Awardees work in close consultation with HUD, and in coordination with other awardees, to help small-community government officials and staff better meet local needs. Applicants must show capacity in one of two categories:

• Category N: TA across HUD's full jurisdiction.

• Category L: TA to specific areas the NOFO will define.

Listed funding activities span business and commerce, community development, housing, and Opportunity Zone benefits. Relevant to TA-provider and consulting clients with small-city, rural, or persistent-poverty experience.
grants.Primary Sector: Community Development Technical Assistance; Local Government Capacity Building; Housing; Economic Development
grants.Link to NOFO: DCTA forecast on Simpler.Grants.gov; HUD User DCTA program page; Grants.gov listing

grants.Description: California Transportation Commission — 2026 Local Partnership Competitive Program (LPP)
grants.Opportunity #: California Grants Portal ID 192465. Competitive Funding Opportunity (CFO); no Cal OES solicitation number shown.
grants.Agency / Funder: California Governor's Office of Emergency Services (Cal OES). Contact NGWSgrantprogram@caloes.ca.gov, 650-218-9422.
grants.Award Range: Up to $750,000 per award; one to two awards expected.
grants.Eligible Applicants:
Businesses only — streaming companies or their affiliates. Statewide.

This is a different applicant pool from Cal OES's earlier FY 2025 NGWS CFO (due May 22, 2026), which was limited to California cities, counties, special districts, and Tribes registered as IPAWS alerting authorities.
grants.Deadline:
November 25, 2026, 5:00 p.m., through Cal OES Intelligrants. This is the day before Thanksgiving; plan to submit early. Opened October 1, 2026.

Expected award announcement December 21, 2026. Period of performance January 1, 2027 – June 30, 2028.
grants.Program Focus:
Next-generation early-warning projects that deliver incident and disaster warnings, including earthquake early warning, to the community and public through streaming services. NGWS is a federal alert-and-warning program supporting delivery of public warnings through existing and new distribution pathways.

The portal's guidelines link opens the Intelligrants home page rather than a CFO document; pull the full CFO from Intelligrants or Cal OES before scoping. Relevant to media, streaming, and alert-technology clients.
grants.Funding Instrument: Grant subaward of federal funds, paid on reimbursement. No letter of intent required.
grants.Primary Sector: Emergency Alert and Warning; Earthquake Early Warning; Streaming and Media Technology; Disaster Preparedness

grants.Description: U.S. Department of Labor, ETA — FY 2027 State Workforce Agency Unemployment Insurance Resource Planning Targets and Guidelines (UIPL 15-26)
grants.Reference #: ETA-UIPL-15-26; Assistance Listing 17.225 (Unemployment Insurance). Grants.gov opportunity 363997.
grants.Issuing Agency: U.S. Department of Labor — Employment and Training Administration. Questions to Rahel Bizuayene, bizuayene.rahel@dol.gov.
grants.Effective Date: Posted September 30, 2026; the listing closes October 30, 2026.
grants.Summary: Preliminary FY 2027 UI State Administration base resource planning targets, general resource-planning guidelines, and an explanation of how DOL allocates base resources among the states. The listing totals $2,632,033,000 in formula funds across 53 jurisdictions, ranging from $1,891,183 to $457,710,985.
grants.Who It Affects: State workforce agencies in the 50 states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico, and the U.S. Virgin Islands. Not a competitive opportunity.
grants.GMA Action Items: None for applications. Useful background for workforce clients that subcontract with state UI agencies, and for the Puerto Rico portfolio, since Puerto Rico's UI administration allocation is set here.

grants.Description: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency — General Terms and Conditions Effective October 1, 2026 or Later
grants.Reference #: EPA General Terms and Conditions, FY 2027 edition (43 pages). The revision-history table is blank as of publication.
grants.Effective Date: October 1, 2026. They apply to new awards, and to existing awards when EPA next adds incremental or supplemental funding. They do not reach expenditures made before that funding action.
grants.Summary:
Provisions most likely to affect client budgets and compliance:

• Termination — EPA may terminate if an award "no longer effectuates the program goals or agency priorities" (2 CFR 200.340(a)(4)).

• Drones — new Term 7 bars EPA funds and cost share from FASC-prohibited unmanned aircraft systems and requires a documented screening check (see RAIN-2027-G01 below).

• Payments — ASAP enrollment required; non-state recipients must disburse drawn funds within five business days.

• Costs — individual consultant pay capped at the Executive Schedule Level IV daily rate; management fees unallowable; indirect costs require a current rate or a de minimis rate of up to 15% of MTDC.

• Subawards — pass-throughs certify to a 16-item subaward management system by accepting the award.

• Reporting — annual SF-425 (due 90 days after period end); final reports due 120 days after the period of performance; Single Audit at $1,000,000 in federal expenditures.

• DBE — the six good-faith efforts remain, but MBE/WBE certification, fair-share objectives, and MBE/WBE reporting stay suspended.

• Acknowledgment — the required funding disclaimer now also disclaims content created with generative AI tools.

• Extensions — no automatic one-time extension; requests are due at least 10 days before the period of performance ends.
grants.Who It Affects: All EPA assistance recipients and subrecipients, including SRF borrowers where noted. Most immediately relevant to the DERA National applicants flagged in last week's digest.
grants.GMA Action Items: Compare against the FY 2026 terms before the next EPA award or amendment for any client; EPA did not publish a redline. Update budget templates for the consultant cap and indirect-cost rules, and add the generative-AI language to client acknowledgment templates.
grants.Link to Source: EPA General Terms and Conditions (PDF); EPA Grant Terms and Conditions page

grants.Description: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency — RAIN-2027-G01: Prohibition on the Purchase and Operation of FASC-Prohibited Unmanned Aircraft Systems
grants.Reference #: RAIN-2027-G01. Implements OMB Memorandum M-26-02 (November 21, 2025) and section 1825 of the American Security Drone Act of 2023 (Pub. L. 118-31).
grants.Effective Date: Notification date October 1, 2026; effective retroactively to December 22, 2025.
grants.Summary:
EPA recipients and subrecipients may not use EPA financial assistance to buy, operate, or use FASC-prohibited unmanned aircraft systems — those made or assembled by a covered foreign entity on the FASC list published in SAM.gov. The bar reaches drones already purchased and in use on an EPA award, and extends to borrowers under EPA-funded revolving loan funds.

To verify a drone, check the FASC Covered Foreign Entity List in SAM.gov, which points to the Consolidated Screening List, and search the manufacturer. Keep a file record showing the search date, the manufacturer and model checked, and the result.
grants.Who It Affects: All EPA recipients and subrecipients, including SRF borrowers. Pass-through entities are solely responsible for flowing the requirement down.
grants.GMA Action Items: Inventory drones used on active client EPA awards (monitoring, mapping, wetland and site surveys), run and document the screening check now, and add the requirement to subaward templates. Note that the EPA web page's summary text mislabels this RAIN as an intergovernmental-review notice; the posted RAIN text and PDF are about drones.

grants.Description: National Academies — Evaluation of ARPA-E's Mission and Goals (Consensus Study Report)
grants.Reference #: NASEM project DEPS-BEES-23-06; congressionally mandated by the Energy Act of 2020. Second NASEM review of ARPA-E (the first was published in 2017).
grants.Issuing Agency: National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine — Committee on the Evaluation of ARPA-E's Mission and Goals (chair Gary Marchant, Arizona State University). Sponsored by DOE.
grants.Effective Date: Report released August 20, 2026. Advisory only; no regulatory effect.
grants.Summary:
The committee found ARPA-E plays a unique role in U.S. energy innovation, de-risking new technologies and drawing in private investment. Selected applicants show more patents and follow-on funding than applicants who were not selected. Key recommendations:

• Congress should keep funding ARPA-E reliably, and raise SCALEUP from roughly $40 million to $120 million per year, on top of the base budget.

• ARPA-E should adopt a proactive program-director hiring strategy spanning career stages, since hiring has drifted toward late-career and national-lab backgrounds and away from startup and industry experience.

• ARPA-E should better measure and communicate broader impacts, including lessons from projects that missed milestones.
grants.Who It Affects: ARPA-E applicants and prior awardees, particularly clients that may be SCALEUP candidates; energy-technology startups planning DOE funding strategy.
grants.GMA Action Items: Use as context for FY 2027 ARPA-E appropriations and as supporting language in ARPA-E applications. Flag clients with prior ARPA-E awards as potential SCALEUP candidates if Congress acts on the funding recommendation.
